title: Per-tenant geo-affinity + retention lifecycle with automated evidence bundles for Hosted API
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers operating under data residency regulations need per-tenant guarantees not only for where requests are served but also for how long transient and persistent artifacts (request payloads, logs, KV cache snapshots, analytics) are retained. Current 'region routing' prototypes do not expose tenant-level retention controls or produce repeatable evidence packages for audits.

Goal: Ship a Per-Tenant Geo-Affinity and Retention Lifecycle capability for the Hosted API that: (1) lets customers set geographic affinity at the API-key/tenant level (preference + required), (2) enforces retention windows for request logs, embeddings, and KV cache snapshots, (3) generates signed evidence bundles (exportable ZIP with metadata, hashes, and audit trail) on demand or on schedule for compliance reviews.

Non-goals: This scope does NOT include Dedicated/VPC on-prem enforcement mechanisms (separate initiative) nor does it change runtime fallback behavior beyond affinity constraints. We will not implement cross-region replication for storage in this quarter.
acceptance_criteria: Admin UI: Tenant settings page exposes 'Geo affinity' with options: Preferred (soft), Required (hard), and Allowed regions list
Retention UI: Per-tenant retention policy UI that sets retention for: request logs, embeddings, metrics, and KV cache snapshots
Enforcement: Requests for tenants marked 'Required' must not be routed outside allowed regions; violations result in 403 with clear error and audit log

Evidence Bundles: Operator can generate an evidence bundle for a tenant for a date range containing: signed manifest, list of routed regions for each request, storage object hashes (sha256), and human-readable summary
API: Expose admin endpoints: GET /admin/tenants/:id/residency, PATCH to update, and POST /admin/tenants/:id/evidence?from=&to= returning presigned download
SLOs: Adding residency enforcement must not increase median p99 latency by >5% in production perf tests
Tests: End-to-end test harness validates routing, retention TTL enforcement, and evidence bundle integrity (sha256) in CI
implementation_notes:
High-level plan:
- PM to finalize UX copy and error surface (this ticket) -> DES-4213 will own mockups.
- ENG to implement routing enforcement middleware and retention enforcement: split into ENG-9271 (routing checks + policy store) and ENG-9348 (retention TTL jobs + immutable retention marks).
- Storage: Use existing audit-bucket pattern, add per-tenant prefix and signed manifests; add metadata headers with region and processing node id.
- Evidence export: small service (stateless lambda-like) that composes objects, computes sha256, signs manifest with platform key, and uploads bundle to presigned S3 link.
- Telemetry: Console to show 'last evidence generated' timestamp and retention compliance percent.
- Security: HSM/KMS signing integration required (sec review).
qa_plan: QA should run the end-to-end harness in staging with 3 synthetic tenants: (A) Preferred=us, Allowed=us,eu (B) Required=eu only (C) Preferred=apac. Verify routing decisions, retention garbage collection, and evidence bundle contents. Additional fuzz tests to simulate region outage and verify error path. Include regression tests for existing routing fallbacks.
rollout_plan: Start with a beta group of 5 tenants (opt-in). Enable policy-check-only mode (logs violations but does not block) for 48h, then flip to enforcement for beta. Monitor routing error rate, latency, and customer support tickets. Gradually expand by 10x every week pending metrics. Notify customers via Console feature flag and email when enforcement is on.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Strict enforcement could block legitimate traffic if model variant not available in region. Mitigation: policy can specify fallbacks and 'required' status defaults to 'preferred' until tenant confirms. Risk: Evidence bundles leak secrets if storage metadata exposed. Mitigation: bundles omit PII, use signed manifests only, and access controlled presigned links with short TTL.
